title: When the Yearbook Falls
premise: Astrid Thackeray transfers to Hollowmere High, a school built over the ruins of a burned-down orphanage, and discovers her late grandmother's recipe box contains instructions for a ritual that lets the reader walk through other people's memories. Using it, she uncovers that the school's beloved founding family covered up a fire they set decades ago to destroy evidence of abuse — a crime still protected by the town's most powerful families. As Astrid and her new friends use borrowed memories to gather proof, the founders' descendants close in, willing to burn the truth again. In the end Astrid must choose between keeping the memories private to protect herself or releasing them publicly, and she chooses justice: the archive opens, the guilty fall, and the orphanage's children are finally named.
about_author: Emrys Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent five years cataloguing the papers of defunct Midwestern institutions. They write young adult fiction about ordinary teenagers who find extraordinary things in filing cabinets.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She arrives at Hollowmere High mid-year, performing cheerfulness for her grieving mother while noting the school's odd architecture — a wing that matches no blueprint. Emotional beat: loneliness masked as adaptability.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Still Astrid. Unpacking grandma's kitchen boxes, she finds index cards among the recipes with instructions that read like directions for a person, not a dish: 'stand where the stairs used to be.' Beat: unease sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: Where the Stairs Used to Be
chapters.summary: Astrid follows card one to the school basement after hours and touches a wall that isn't a wall. She experiences a stranger's memory — a boy named Tobias, 1954, smoke. Beat: terror and wonder entwined.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Isn't in Any Photo
chapters.summary: Astrid researches Tobias Hale and finds him erased from every yearbook. Librarian Ms. Okonkwo notices her digging and warns her off without explaining. Beat: first hint the silence is maintained on purpose.

chapters.title: Labels Off
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Dev, a scholarship kid Astrid befriended, who catches her sneaking back to the basement and demands the truth. He tests the memory-wall himself and sees his own absent father's past. Beat: reluctant alliance formed.

chapters.title: Card Seven: Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The recipe cards form a sequence; card seven requires something burned from the original building. The pair realize someone else has been using the cards — one is missing. Beat: they are not alone.

chapters.title: The Founders' Wing
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. They investigate the Whitlock family, whose name is on half the school, and meet golden-boy Eli Whitlock, who seems genuinely kind — and genuinely frightened when Astrid mentions the orphanage. Beat: sympathy complicating suspicion.

chapters.title: What Priya Saw
chapters.summary: New POV: Priya, editor of the yearbook, has found a 1954 volume with pages razored out. She joins them, bringing archival skills and a personal stake — her grandmother was an orphanage resident. Beat: the team becomes three.

chapters.title: Borrowed Grief
chapters.summary: Astrid overuses the memory-wall and comes back carrying Tobias's fear as her own, snapping at her mother. Dev pulls her back with a grounding ritual of his own invention. Beat: cost of power made intimate.

chapters.title: The Fire Was Set
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Piecing together razored pages and a memory of the night itself, they confirm: the orphanage burned deliberately, killing three children, to hide abuse ledgers. The Whitlocks were there. Beat: horror hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Eli's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Eli confronts Astrid: he knows what his great-grandfather did; he's been trying to decide what to do about it for years. He reveals the missing recipe card was taken by his uncle Marcus, who uses it to keep secrets buried. Beat: an ally inside the enemy house.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Archive
chapters.summary: The four break into the county records annex to copy surviving ledgers. Marcus catches them but can't act publicly without exposing himself; instead he threatens Astrid's mother's job. Beat: power shows its face — quiet, legal, ruthless.

chapters.title: Fine Is a Lie
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Her mother discovers her bruises and sleeplessness; Astrid almost tells everything, then lies again. Alone, she reads grandma's final card: 'Memory kept secret rots. Memory shared becomes history.' Beat: guilt and clarity.

chapters.title: The Yearbook Falls Open
chapters.summary: Priya publishes a teaser spread: the razored 1954 yearbook, restored digitally, names redacted — bait. The town erupts; Marcus moves to have Priya expelled. Beat: point of no return; the hunt reverses direction.

chapters.title: Smoke Again
chapters.summary: Someone sets a small fire in the archive wing — a message. Astrid reaches through the wall and finds the memory-space fraying, as if the past itself is being edited. Beat: dread; the stakes turn supernatural-adjacent and immediate.

chapters.title: Card Twelve: What You're Willing to Lose
chapters.summary: The final card requires a memory of the user's own, given up permanently. Astrid realizes the ritual's true price and hides this from the others. Beat: sacrifice foreshadowed; isolation deepens.

chapters.title: Marcus's Version
chapters.summary: Marcus offers Astrid a deal: the memory-wall's full power, her mother's security, in exchange for the cards and silence. He shows her a memory of his own — a child he failed to save — muddying easy villainy. Beat: temptation with a human face.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: The four argue about going public: Dev fears exposure of his father, Priya fears losing college prospects, Eli fears destroying his family entirely. Astrid refuses to decide alone. Beat: fracture before unity; trust tested honestly.

chapters.title: Hollowmere Burns Brightest at Night
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Marcus breaks into the basement to destroy the wall; the kids race him, and Astrid gives up her happiest memory — a summer day with grandma — to anchor the space against his edits. Beat: sacrifice paid; chaos and courage.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Climax resolves. With Eli testifying against his own family, the full record goes public: the three dead children are named — Tobias among them — and Marcus is arrested for arson and obstruction. Beat: catharsis; justice outside the law completed by law at last.

chapters.title: Aftertaste
chapters.summary: Falling action. Astrid grieves the lost summer day she can no longer remember, comforted by friends who remember it for her. Her mother finally hears the whole story. Beat: bittersweet tenderness; memory as shared burden.

chapters.title: The New Yearbook
chapters.summary: Resolution. Spring: the school installs a memorial wing with the orphans' names; Priya's staff prints a corrected edition. Astrid adds one blank page at the back — for whatever comes next. Beat: hope, continuity, and the theme sealed: labels off, people remembered.
